newsitem.title: GERMANY: German March unemployment falls to 4.30 million.
newsitem.headline: German March unemployment falls to 4.30 million.

text.p: German unemployment fell to a seasonally adjusted 4.30 million in March, the Federal Labour Office said on Tuesday.
The unemployment rate, which is based on unadjusted data, fell to 11.7 percent, compared with 12.2 percent in February. The number of unemployed workers fell by an adjusted 15,000 from February.

"There were many job losses in the early part of the year above all because of bad weather...The exceptionally mild weather in March made rehiring workers in outdoor jobs easier," said the president of the Labour Office, Bernhard Jagoda.
Independent analysts had expected a fall of between 15,000 and 25,000 in seasonally-adjusted unemployment after unadjusted figures were leaked on Monday.
Unadjusted unemployment -- the most politically sensitive jobs figure in Germany -- fell by around 190,000 to 4.48 million from February's 4.67 million, the highest since 1933.
In western Germany, the number of people out of work on a seasonally adjusted basis rose by 1,000 to 3.014 million in March from 3.013 million in February.
In eastern Germany, the adjusted number of unemployed fell by 16,000 to 1.284 million.
